content.title: About
content.content: Bison, ground, raw is finely minced bison meat that has not been cooked. The raw grind retains the natural flavor and tenderness of the meat, offering a high‑protein, nutrient‑dense ingredient for a variety of dishes such as burgers, meatballs, and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground bison is a staple in many North American indigenous cuisines.
Raw meat preserves more B‑vitamins compared with cooked meat.
Bison meat has a slightly sweeter taste than beef due to lower fat content.
Bison farming has a smaller environmental footprint than traditional cattle ranching.
In some regions, raw ground bison is used to make traditional dishes like “bison tartare.”

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground bison provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: The iron in bison is highly bioavailable and helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Lean bison offers modest amounts of omega‑3s, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Mineral source
items.content: Provides zinc and selenium, which support immune function.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw ground meat can harbor pathogens such as Salmonella and E. coli. Keep it refrigerated at 0‑4 °C and cook thoroughly.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to bison proteins.

items.title: Higher fat content than lean cuts
items.content: Ground bison can contain up to 15 % fat, increasing calorie density.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large portions of raw ground meat may cause digestive discomfort in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw ground bison should only be used in recipes where it will be fully cooked: burgers, meatballs, stews, or baked dishes. Do not consume it raw.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the ground meat in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
